rows.uncertainty: Abstract only; full text subscription only (paywall list). No patient, lesion or biopsy counts, no p-values or statistical test, no follow-up beyond the repigmentation time. Number of freezing sessions not in abstract, so the 6 to 8 weeks cannot be placed relative to the final treatment and months after final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE. Overlapping authors (Dee-Ananlap S, Suvanprakorn P) with suvanprakorn1985, a different intervention; no shared cohort stated. 'Lesions gently frozen with liquid nitrogen repigmented' does not say whether all or some lesions repigmented, nor whether repigmentation was partial or complete; it is not recorded as complete area coverage or colour match. Repigmented areas held fewer dopa-positive melanocytes than normal skin (histology row), which [may bear on colour match and durability] but the abstract does not say so. Adverse effects (blister, hyperpigmented halo, scar) not in abstract.

The baseline finding (fewer dopa-positive melanocytes in IGH macules than normal skin; round, less dendritic melanocytes with fewer melanosomes on electron microscopy) is a pre-treatment description, not a treatment outcome. Repigmented areas remained below normal skin melanocyte numbers.
